name: Lost at Sea with an AI moderator
author: Human Not Found
description: Original study: Conte, S. P. (2026). AI Moderation in Multi-Party Voice Conversations: Architecture, Strategies, and Evaluation (Master's thesis, Politecnico di Milano). Ten groups of three ranked 15 items alone, then discussed by voice for up to 30 minutes under the consensus ground rules of Hall & Watson (1970) and submitted one group ranking, once with an AI moderator that balanced participation and enforced the ground rules, and once without it. Each group did NASA Moon Survival in one session and Lost at Sea in the other, with task and moderator order counterbalanced. Rankings were scored against the expert ranking (error score, lower is better) and against the group's own members (synergy); participation balance was the Gini index of floor-holding time. In this template three members with personas (a talkative engineering student, an office administrator who takes part at an ordinary pace and a reserved shop assistant; the personas are ours, not the thesis's) rank the items alone and privately, discuss in text with the ground rules, speaking when they raise a hand (up to 15 member turns), and then the first member submits the group ranking. In the 'Moderator on' condition an AI moderator joins the discussion: it invites the quietest member when participation gets uneven and gently recalls a ground rule when a message breaks one; it does not rank. In 'Moderator off' it is disabled and the ground rules are only stated at the start. Participation inequality uses the thesis's Gini formula on the members' words, which stand in for floor-holding time in a text discussion. Run this template and its sibling (NASA Moon Survival with an AI moderator) together to reproduce the within-group design; every repetition uses the same three personas, so repetitions differ only through the model's own variation. Participants are simulated: each is a Model participant, using the free test model until you choose a model, so the first runs only check the design; with the test model every participant takes the sample answer.

config.ground_rules: 1. Avoid arguing for your own ranking: present your position clearly and logically, but seriously consider the group's reactions. 2. Avoid win-lose stalemates: when you reach an impasse, look for the next most acceptable alternative for everyone. 3. Do not change your mind only to avoid conflict; resist pressure to yield that has no sound basis. 4. Avoid conflict-reducing techniques such as majority vote, averaging, bargaining or coin flipping; treat differences of opinion as a sign that information is still missing, and ask for it. 5. See differences of opinion as natural and helpful, not as an obstacle. 6. Treat initial agreement as suspect: check that people agree for the same or complementary reasons.
config.instructions: The group is doing the Lost at Sea task and must agree on one shared ranking.

research.question: Does an AI moderator that balances participation and enforces consensus ground rules change the quality of the group's decision and how evenly members take part?

config.prompt: You chartered a yacht with three friends to cross the Atlantic. In mid-Atlantic a fire broke out; the skipper and crew were lost fighting it, the yacht is slowly sinking, and the navigation and radio equipment are destroyed. You are probably many hundreds of miles from land. You saved 15 intact items, along with a life raft and a box of matches. Rank the items by their importance while you wait to be rescued: 1 is the most important.
